terms.gloss: a trailer (a cart that is pulled)
terms.comment: Our description: a cart that is pulled. Morgan–Owens has currus remulcātus under “trailer, caravan, RV” (below), the kind one lives in, and gives no Latin under its heading for a truck’s trailer; Traupman has only the trailer home. So for a trailer that carries a load the description stays.

terms.gloss: a trailer, a caravan (the kind one lives in)
terms.comment: Egger’s phrase, “a towed vehicle”. Remulcāre is not in Lewis & Short, which has remulcum, a tow-rope.
Traupman’s phrase, “a towed dwelling”: habitāculum is late Latin for a dwelling (Lewis & Short), and remulcāre is not in Lewis & Short.

sources: Descriptions and prompts labelled as ours are composed for family conversation. Recorded vocabulary does not imply universal technical standardization.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. trailer, caravan, RV.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 397.
